item.title: RT: 标普 500 指数今年已有 27 个大幅下跌日（>1%）和 27 个大幅上涨日（>1%）。 历史表明
item.description:
标普 500 指数今年已有 27 个大幅下跌日（>1%）和 27 个大幅上涨日（>1%）。

历史表明，两者是齐头并进的。

波动性是股票市场的一个特征，而不是缺陷。从长远来看，这是股票比债券/现金获得更高回报的主要原因。

The S&P 500 has now had 27 big down days (>1%) this year and 27 big up days (>1%).

History shows that the two go hand in hand.

Volatility is a feature of stock markets, not a bug. It's the primary reason why stocks have earned a higher return than bonds/cash over the long run.

item.title: RT: 加息以降低通胀并不是“政策错误”，而是美联储的首要任务。真正的政策错误是认为零利率
item.description:
加息以降低通胀并不是“政策错误”，而是美联储的首要任务。真正的政策错误是认为零利率、在房地产泡沫中购买数万亿抵押贷款债券以及在两年内将货币供应量增加 40% 不会产生负面后果。

Hiking rates to bring down inflation is not a "policy mistake," it's the Fed's #1 job. The true policy mistake was believing that 0% rates, buying trillions of mortgage bonds in a housing bubble & increasing the money supply by 40% in 2 years would have no negative consequences.

@BillAckman

我认为美联储将在 12 月 9 日犯下另一个错误。金融状况大幅收紧。例如，投资级公司 @SpaceX 刚刚以 8.259% 的利率筹集了有担保债务融资，而其 IPO 时无担保债券发行的利率低于 6%。

随着近期股市大幅下跌，股本成本也大幅上升。

美联储 2% 的通胀目标是错误的。地缘政治风险和全球军费开支、去全球化和关税所需的投资，以及大规模的人工智能基础设施和相关能源投资，这些都是设定2%目标时不存在的世界特征。 3%的通胀率是新世界更现实的目标。

如果美联储在将通胀率推至2%的尝试失败后继续加息，将使美国和世界陷入衰退。

告诉我为什么我错了。

I think the Fed is about to make another mistake on December 9th. Financial conditions have tightened massively. For example, @SpaceX, an investment grade company, just raised secured debt financing at an 8.259% interest rate versus below 6% for its unsecured bond offering at the time of its IPO.

The cost of equity capital has also increased materially with the recent substantial decline in the stock market.

The Fed’s 2% inflation ambition is misguided. Geopolitical risk and the required investment in global military spending, de globalization and tariffs, and the massive AI infrastructure and related energy investment are features of the world that did not exist when the 2% target was set. 3% inflation is a more realistic ambition in the new world.

The Fed will put the U.S. and world in recession if it continues to raise rates in a failed attempt to drive inflation to 2%.

Tell me why I am wrong.
